what_it_does: Detecting small objects in very high-resolution images (2-megapixel video frames) is computationally expensive and demands enormous memory bandwidth. This paper presents a specialized CNN (convolutional neural network) processor designed for exactly this task. The key insight is that many small objects appear at different scales, so the processor uses a bidirectional feature pyramid—a technique that extracts features at multiple zoom levels, then combines them. To fit within a mobile chip's power and memory budget, the design introduces three innovations: a memory-efficient way to compute features bidirectionally by rearranging pixel order, a smart backbone scheduling scheme that recomputes intermediate values instead of storing them, and a reconfigurable math engine that adapts to different layer types. Running at 5.7 trillion operations per second, it enables real-time small-object detection on edge devices.
